newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa rebounds off new lows to end higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa rebounds off new lows to end higher.

text.p: CSCE nearby cocoa prices bounced back from contract lows set early in the day to end higher Thursday, as locals and commission houses covered short positions, floor sources said.
In what dealers said was mainly a technical consolidation following this morning's collapse to 10-month lows, spot March delivery shot up $26, to a peak of $1,298.

By the close, March delivery stood at $1,287 a tonne, up $15 a tonne, after sinking to a fresh life-of-contract low of $1,255 eraly in the day. Active May closed up $11, to $1,317, while the outer months finished $9 to $12 higher.
Prices took a downturn at the outset, as operators followed through on two consecutive sessions of sharp losses. Prices slid nearly $20 before the ring began to cover their short positions.
"It was a good comeback," said Rich Wistisen, an analyst with Commodity Information in Orem, Utah. "Technically, it was a very encouraging bounce, but it needs to rebound more than one day."
Wistisen said a break above $1,330 in the March contract would signal a clearer turnaround on the charts. But he said the market's fundamental outlook was likely to continue to pressure the market.

The increase in the pace of arrivals out of the Ivory Coast may point to a larger-than-expected harvest, he said. Additionally, last year's huge crop is likely to help offset any world cocoa deficit in 1996/97.
"We are still seeing the glut of last year's massive crop weighing on the market," Wistisen said.
Volume Thursday was brisk, at an estimated 13,108 lots.
